highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.156.0 improves platform integration, rendering reliability, and allocation behavior across managed and native code.
highlights_body: The release updates platform support for Apple, Windows, Linux, Android, and WebAssembly while reducing overhead in image processing, text shaping, and stream handling.

bullets.lead: C string data is copied safely
bullets.detail: SKData creation from a C string now reads the intended buffer directly, preventing reads past the native string boundary.

bullets.lead: Android texture rendering follows display refresh
bullets.detail: Texture rendering on Android is synchronized with the display refresh cycle for more reliable frame presentation.

bullets.lead: Image and text processing allocate less
bullets.detail: Managed image pixel copies, HarfBuzz UTF-32 encoding, and native feature-string processing avoid unnecessary allocations in common processing paths.
Front-buffered streams no longer retain buffered content longer than necessary.
Apple-targeted applications now require the updated minimum deployment versions supported by the 4.156 line.

bullets.lead: Windows native dependencies align with MAUI
bullets.detail: Windows native assets now align with the dependency sets used by MAUI 9 and MAUI 10.

bullets.lead: Native WebGPU and Linux HarfBuzz integration is improved
bullets.detail: WebAssembly packages include the emdawnwebgpu implementation, while Linux loads bundled HarfBuzz functions locally.

contributor_summaries.VirgilMing: Improved Linux binding of bundled HarfBuzz functions and stabilized Blazor CPU sample rendering tests
contributor_summaries.dalexsoto: Addressed contextual policy findings in the continuous-integration configuration
contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Included the emdawnwebgpu implementation in the native WebAssembly library
